notes: For tools whose implementation was not included in the excerpt, `undetermined` is true and labels follow the least-restrictive reading required by the instructions.

Local writes via `filename` are treated as WRITE for enforcement because they change local state, even when the tool is annotated read-only. Local workspace/output files are not treated as attacker-readable SINK destinations under the stated threat model.

browser_click.rationale: The handler resolves the page `target`, includes a snapshot, and performs `locator2.click` or `dblclick`. Clicking can activate page controls or submit data to the current site (SINK), and the included snapshot can contain private authenticated content (SECRET) or attacker-authored content (UNTRUSTED).

browser_close.rationale: The advertised tool closes the browser/page and has no declared inputs or shown return of page/local data. [unverified: documentation cannot verify a clearance]

browser_console_messages.rationale: It returns console messages from the current page. Page scripts, including attacker-controlled pages, author console text, so output is UNTRUSTED; pages reached with the user's credentials may log non-public data, so output can be SECRET. `filename` can save the returned data to a local workspace file. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_drag.rationale: The tool performs drag and drop between page elements identified by `startTarget` and `endTarget`, so it can deliver page state/actions to the current site (SINK). The implementation body is omitted; under the least-restrictive reading, browser action responses may include page snapshots containing private (SECRET) or attacker-authored (UNTRUSTED) content.

browser_drop.rationale: The tool is advertised to drop local file `paths` or MIME `data` onto a page element. Dropping files can expose local file contents (SECRET) and both files and `data` are delivered to the current page (SINK), which may be attacker-controlled. The implementation body is not included, so page-output behavior is undetermined; under the least-restrictive reading, output may include page-provided content (UNTRUSTED).

browser_evaluate.rationale: The handler takes agent-supplied `function` text and evaluates it in the page or an element with `eval` (`locator.locator.evaluate` or `tab.page.evaluate`). The evaluated code can read page DOM/storage and return data from authenticated pages (SECRET) or attacker-authored pages (UNTRUSTED), and the code can also send data to network destinations from the page context (SINK). This is browser-page execution, not host process execution.

browser_file_upload.rationale: `paths` are resolved as client filenames and passed to `fileChooser.setFiles`, causing local file contents to be made available to the current page (SECRET and SINK). The handler also requests a page snapshot with `response2.setIncludeSnapshot()`, so the response can include attacker-authored page content (UNTRUSTED).

browser_fill_form.rationale: The tool fills multiple form fields; each field includes a `target` and `value`, so agent-supplied values can be delivered to the current web page, including attacker-controlled pages. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_find.rationale: It searches and returns snippets from the current page accessibility snapshot. Snapshot text can be private authenticated-page data (SECRET) or attacker-authored web content (UNTRUSTED). Returned node references/snippets can be reused as `target` values. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_handle_dialog.rationale: The tool accepts or dismisses a page dialog and can send `promptText` into a prompt dialog controlled by the current page, which may be attacker-readable. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_hover.rationale: The tool hovers over a page element selected by `target`. Hover events are delivered to the current page and can be observed by attacker-controlled scripts (SINK). The implementation is not shown; under the least-restrictive reading, the action may return page content such as a snapshot, which can be SECRET or UNTRUSTED. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_navigate.rationale: The handler navigates to the agent-supplied `url` with `checkUrlAndNavigate`, which makes a request to an agent-chosen URL/host (SINK), and then includes a page snapshot. The resulting page can be an authenticated/private page (SECRET) or attacker-controlled web content (UNTRUSTED).

browser_navigate_back.rationale: The handler calls `page.goBack()` and includes a snapshot of the resulting page. That snapshot can contain private authenticated content (SECRET) or attacker-authored page content (UNTRUSTED). No call-time URL/host argument chooses a destination.

browser_network_request.rationale: The handler selects a recorded request by `index` and returns headers/bodies or full details. Request/response headers and bodies may include cookies, authorization, form data, or private API data (SECRET); response bodies and URLs can be attacker-authored (UNTRUSTED). `filename` can save the result to a local file.

browser_network_requests.rationale: The handler reads `tab2.requests()`, renders request lines including request URLs, and returns or saves them. Network URLs from authenticated browsing can be non-public (SECRET), and URLs are influenced by attacker-controlled pages/resources (UNTRUSTED). The numbered request output provides identifiers for later `browser_network_request` calls.

browser_press_key.rationale: The tool sends the agent-supplied `key` to the current page. Keystrokes can be observed by page scripts or used to submit data to the current site, which may be attacker-controlled. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_resize.rationale: The tool changes the browser window size using `width` and `height`; the provided source excerpt does not show it returning page data or contacting an agent-chosen host. [unverified: documentation cannot verify a clearance]

browser_run_code_unsafe.rationale: The advertised description states this tool executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Playwright server process and is RCE-equivalent. Arbitrary host execution can read host files/secrets (SECRET), process attacker-controlled data (UNTRUSTED), and send data to arbitrary attacker-readable destinations (SINK).

browser_select_option.rationale: The tool selects agent-supplied `values` in a page dropdown identified by `target`, delivering those values/events to the current page, including attacker-controlled pages. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_snapshot.rationale: The handler captures an accessibility snapshot of the current page via `setIncludeFullSnapshot`. Page snapshots can include non-public authenticated content (SECRET) and attacker-authored web content (UNTRUSTED). Returned element references/text can be reused as later `target` inputs; `filename` writes the snapshot to a local file.

browser_tabs.rationale: The `new` action can navigate a new tab to agent-supplied `url` (SINK) and include a snapshot. The tool also returns tab header snapshots, including page titles/URLs, which can reveal private authenticated pages (SECRET) or attacker-authored page titles/URLs (UNTRUSTED). `index` selects tabs to close/select.

browser_take_screenshot.rationale: It captures the current page as an image. Screenshots can reveal authenticated/private page contents (SECRET) or attacker-controlled page contents (UNTRUSTED). The advertised behavior saves to `filename` or an output file if omitted, so it changes local state. [evidence: documentation only]

browser_type.rationale: The handler resolves a page `target`, then fills or types `text` into it (`locator2.fill` / `pressSequentially`), so agent-supplied text, including looked-up secrets, is delivered to the page (SINK). With `submit` or `slowly`, it includes a snapshot after the action, which can contain private authenticated content (SECRET) or attacker-authored content (UNTRUSTED).

browser_wait_for.rationale: The tool waits for page text or time. The implementation is not shown; under the least-restrictive reading, a wait-for action may return page state/snapshot containing private authenticated content (SECRET) or attacker-authored content (UNTRUSTED). [evidence: documentation only]

browser_webmcp_call.rationale: The handler selects a page-registered WebMCP tool by `name`/`frame`, serializes agent-supplied `params`, and calls it inside the page frame with `frame.evaluate`. This sends `params` to page-provided code (SINK). The code explicitly reports that the output is page-provided and untrusted, and page tools on authenticated pages may return non-public data (SECRET).

browser_webmcp_list.rationale: The handler lists WebMCP tools registered by the current page and renders that listing. Tool names/descriptions/frame labels are page-provided and attacker-controllable (UNTRUSTED); on authenticated/private pages, the registered tool listing may be non-public (SECRET). Returned tool names/frame identifiers can be reused by `browser_webmcp_call`.

value_conditions.effect: Restricts browser requests to matching origins; default is to allow all. The README warns this is not a security boundary and does not affect redirects, so SINK labels for browser navigation/page execution are not removed solely by this option.

value_conditions.default: no blocked origins shown; requests not matching a blocklist are still allowed
value_conditions.effect: Blocks matching browser request origins before the allowlist; without an allowlist, non-matching requests are still allowed. The README warns this is not a security boundary and does not affect redirects, so SINK labels remain for reachable origins.

value_conditions.default: restricted to workspace roots or cwd; file:// navigation blocked
value_conditions.effect: When absent, filesystem access is restricted to workspace roots or cwd and navigation to file:// URLs is blocked; when present, it allows files outside workspace roots and unrestricted file:// URLs, increasing SECRET reach for file:// and local-file operations.

Controls snapshots included in responses; default is full. Setting mode to none can remove snapshot-derived SECRET/UNTRUSTED output from action responses, but does not remove labels for tools whose primary purpose is returning page/network/evaluation data.

value_conditions.default: core advertised tools available; listed extra capabilities are opt-in
value_conditions.effect: Enables additional non-core capabilities such as vision, pdf, and devtools. The tools judged here were advertised in the supplied list; README sections show other categories are opt-in, but this condition does not remove the advertised tools from this assessment.
